title: Hussain Shahi Dynasty
capsule: The Hussain Shahi dynasty ruled the Bengal Sultanate from 1494, when Alauddin Husain Shah seized the throne from the Habshi rulers, until the Suri Afghan conquest in 1538. Alauddin (r. 1494–1519) is regarded as the greatest sultan of Bengal: he expanded the sultanate to its largest extent, incorporating Kamata, Jajnagar, and parts of Arakan, and presided over a cultural renaissance that included the commissioning of Sanskrit-to-Bengali literary translations and the patronage of Vaishnavism alongside Islam. His son Nusrat Shah (r. 1519–1532) continued this expansion and concluded the first treaty between Bengal and the Mughal Empire. The dynasty ended in 1538 when Sher Shah Suri defeated Sultan Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah and absorbed Bengal into the Sur Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory of the Hussain Shahi sultanate is well attested through epigraphy and Persian chronicles; its northeastern and eastern frontier zones in Arakan and Assam are less precisely delimited.
